title: Evidence map for q-0020 through q-0023 policy/runtime defaults
scope: Map draft security, owner-routing, runtime-family, and execution-evidence defaults to existing PM Plans precedent first and Coasts source-lineage second, preserving open user acceptance.
precedence_rule: PM canonical owner docs win conflicts. Coasts/Coast Guard is source-lineage inspiration only where compatible.

evidence_map.conclusion: PM already requires pre-dispatch permission checks, discovery-not-approval, explicit host/registry/cluster trust outcomes, fail-closed FileSafe scope handling, remote-side-effect receipts, sensitive metadata masking, no-persist/no-echo secret handling, browser profile isolation, and artifact privacy/retention policy. Coasts confirms these are real risk surfaces through privileged DinD, secrets extraction/injection, ports/egress, volume strategies, and Keychain tests. Accept as PM safety defaults, not as Coasts-derived canon and not as a generic privileged-runtime trust model.
conflicts_or_caveats: Do not describe privileged runtime support as a broad trusted mode; privileged/host-mutating modes require scoped permission, trust/proxy/host-policy checks, capability/preflight evidence, and non-bypassable approval where applicable.

evidence_map.conclusion: PM precedent supports a split owner model: Containers/Docker Manager owns the native Docker/Hosts operational behavior and container lifecycle, FinalGUI consumes placement/shell vocabulary, UI_Command_Catalog owns command ids, Tools owns dispatch/tool behavior, Executor owns attempt identity and dispatch evidence, ATS owns testing capability and receipts, Permissions/FileSafe own approval and invocation gates, Runtime Artifacts owns artifact/receipt presentation and retention, Assistant Chat/Orchestrator/Goal Runtime consume the shared runtime identity where their surfaces use hosts. Coasts remains source-lineage only. Jared has already accepted a new native Docker/Hosts page, so the page placement is not reopened; compile must reconcile this with the existing Docker Manager owner vocabulary rather than inventing a separate Hosts owner canon.
conflicts_or_caveats: Containers_Registry_and_Unraid.md:21 still names Plans/newtools.md as canonical for runtime/tool/preflight/evidence behavior. Treat this as stale/source-lineage compatibility or clean it up before compile; do not let it override current owner docs.
Do not promote Coasts, ledger prose, newtools.md compatibility bridges, or stale owner hints into product canon.

Agent review suggested Docker Manager side-panel/subview ownership rather than a new top-level Hosts page; this conflicts with Jared accepted Docker/Hosts page placement and is recorded only as owner-routing evidence, not as a reversal of user intent.
Retire stale GUI hints such as Docker Manage aliases, separate Unraid panel ids, tier_id, and old route-command assumptions as compatibility/source-lineage where current owner docs supersede them.

evidence_map.conclusion: PM supports Docker-first runtime, Compose/Buildx/Bake, Docker Manager, requested/effective capability, preflight-before-approval, HTE-default adapters, explicit DAE only when allowed, project-focused Kubernetes, Unraid publishing, and disabled/blocker states. Coasts is source-lineage compatible for containerized-host patterns such as declarative Coastfile-like config, host/instance/build separation, dynamic/canonical ports, and isolated instances. Coasts is not proof that DinD, Podman, Sysbox, SSH tunnels, custom/command secret extractors, or the Coasts daemon/service model are PM-supported defaults.
conflicts_or_caveats: Do not claim Podman rootless parity from Coasts evidence; Coasts presents Podman as future/not wired in docs, and the local code shows privileged Podman container parameters. Prefer wording: Podman is a capability-probed compatible alternate with limitations visible. Sysbox is the non-privileged/rootless nested-runtime candidate where available.

Reject treating privileged DinD, Sysbox, Podman, SSH tunnels, command/custom secret extractors, or the Coasts daemon/service model as PM-supported defaults without PM-owned validation, explicit host/secret/permission policy, and runtime enablement evidence.

Coasts remote mode has high-risk requirements such as Docker, GatewayPorts, passwordless sudo, privileged coast-service, docker.sock, SSH tunnels, and cleanup commands; PM must route these through explicit host trust, FileSafe, permission, receipt, and blocked-state policy.
Coasts compatibility is evidence for patterns only: Coastfile-like declarations, host/instance/build separation, dynamic/canonical ports, and isolated instances.

evidence_map.conclusion: PM precedent requires dispatch/attempt identity, worktree/cwd binding, permission and blocked-action carrythrough, automated test capability/probe/strategy/receipt evidence, no manual-only completion, runtime artifacts with receipt linkage, retention/redaction, and blocked/failure reason taxonomy. Coasts confirms practical lanes exist for integration tests, agent shells, logs, ports, exec, and runtime-heavy tasks, but PM owns the evidence model rather than copying Coasts terminal/web-UI semantics. Accept where runtime execution is later enabled and authority allows it.
conflicts_or_caveats: Do not imply runtime dispatch, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, or PlanCompile runtime are enabled by this ledger-only planning pass.
Runtime Artifacts is projection/evidence browsing, not receipt truth; stale or missing owner records degrade the view rather than becoming final evidence.
Testing restrictions require explicit durable override and must be marked as approved verification exceptions, not automated passes.

synthesis.overall_recommendation: Ask Jared to accept q-0020 through q-0023 as adjusted evidence-mapped defaults: PM safety defaults for q-0020, canonical owner split with accepted Docker/Hosts page preserved for q-0021, PM runtime defaults plus Coasts-compatible patterns only for q-0022, and runtime-authorized execution/evidence defaults with Runtime Artifacts as projection for q-0023.
true_product_forks_remaining: Whether Jared wants q-0022 wording narrowed now to Podman capability-probed alternate with visible limitations, leaving Sysbox as the rootless/non-privileged nested-runtime candidate.
Whether the stale newtools.md owner note should be cleaned during eventual compile or explicitly routed around in the compile source notes.
Whether q-0020 wording should explicitly say privileged/host-mutating modes are scoped hard-gated operations rather than trusted runtime modes.
Whether q-0023 wording should explicitly say defaults apply only when runtime execution is later enabled and authority allows them, with Runtime Artifacts as projection rather than receipt truth.

Whether q-0021 compile wording should explicitly preserve the accepted new Docker/Hosts page while mapping owner canon through Docker Manager/Containers and FinalGUI rather than a separate Hosts owner.

Whether q-0022 should explicitly reject upstream Coasts privileged DinD, SSH tunnel, command/custom secret extractor, and daemon/service models as PM-supported defaults until PM-owned validation exists.
preserved_negative_constraints: Do not write canonical Plans during this conversational evidence-map pass.
Do not let Coasts override PM canonical owner docs.
Do not claim Podman/Sysbox parity without PM capability probes and blocker states.
Do not enable privileged DinD by default or hide its critical-risk status.
Do not treat host discovery/configuration as execution approval.
Do not claim Coasts as canonical PM authority.
Do not imply runtime dispatch is enabled by a ledger-only planning pass.
Do not make Runtime Artifacts the receipt authority.
Do not reopen Jared accepted Docker/Hosts page placement based on agent owner-routing caveats.
Do not promote newtools.md compatibility bridges or stale owner hints into product canon.
Do not treat Coasts runtime claims as PM-supported runtime evidence.
